summary.text: 上 uses a positional mark above a reference line to indicate “above” or the upper side. Paleographic accounts describe early forms with either a curved or straight baseline; Shang-period uses are reported in 上帝 and 上甲.

formation.text: Indicative: the mark’s position above a reference line indicates the upper side. The received Shuowen text also classifies the graph as indicative; that is a Han-era analysis, not independent evidence for its earlier graphic history.

history.text: Early forms are described as a short mark above a longer reference line, though accounts differ on whether that line was curved or horizontal. Later forms altered the upper mark, often making it vertical to distinguish 上 from 二; the modern standard form has a dot. These are graphic changes, not evidence of a change in meaning.

The received Shuowen text treats 丄 as an ancient form meaning “high” and 上 as its seal-script form. The received text also has an editorial difference over whether its head form is 丄 or 二; this records a lexicographic tradition rather than confirming the Shang graphic history.

uncertainties.text: The earliest graph form discussed is oracle-bone 上, but no earlier dated occurrence is established. The inscriptional examples are reported by paleographic accounts; a photograph of an artifact transcribed with 上甲 does not isolate that character.
Accounts agree on a mark above a reference line but differ on whether the early line was curved or horizontal; no primary inscription image resolves this variation.

Reported uses include spatial “above/upper side” and “at/on the side of,” authority-related meanings, and verbs glossed “ascend” and “send up.” The examples or reconstructed lexical rows do not establish a dated sequence or semantic connections among these uses. A reported 以上 meaning “more than” is a compound use, not evidence for a single-character sense.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone and Zhou bronze inscription contexts reported
senses.text: Reported Shang-period examples include 上帝, 上甲, and contrasts with 下; Zhou bronze examples include spatial “above.” These support early spatial uses but do not establish priority among every lexical use.
A bronze-inscription account reports this spatial use. Its relationship to “above” is not established.
Current dictionary metadata gives spatial and rank-related glosses; the list does not establish their historical sequence.

limitations.text: Early spatial uses are supported, and several other uses are reported, but dated semantic transitions among them are not established. 上帝 and 上甲 are compound examples, not automatically independent senses of 上.

The reported 以上 example means “more than” in a compound and does not establish a single-character sense. Supplied reconstructed phonological rows separately gloss 上 as “ascend,” “put up,” and “top, above”; these rows do not establish attested usage, semantic chronology, or graphic origin.

overview.text: A small mark above a reference line indicates “above” or the upper side. Early forms are described with either a curved or horizontal line, but the positional construction is shared across accounts.
